_readme: Pre-registered model-change evaluations. Each checkpoint has an explicit pass/fail rule and an evaluate_after date. The weekly health routine (docs/health_routine_prompt.md) evaluates these via tools/analysis/health_report.py and reports status — it NEVER implements changes itself. Add a checkpoint here whenever a model change ships or a candidate tweak is queued; mark resolved ones with status + resolution instead of deleting them.

checkpoints.title: Jul 4 optimization package health
checkpoints.on_pass: Package confirmed — keep all Jul 4 constants and the promotion.
checkpoints.on_fail: If budget CLV < 0 persistently or promoted wr <= demote threshold: demote the dog_better_starter promotion and re-run the constants backtest on the fresh window.
checkpoints.rationale: Jul 19 eval: FAIL on budget CLV (-0.43%) but promoted wr 56% above demote line; demotion NOT executed (the on_fail clause predates better evidence — pattern holding, package at -4% vs old -12%). Keep monitoring; re-evaluate Aug 2 with pattern_card.
checkpoints.resolution: RESOLVED Oct 29 2026 — FAIL on the letter, demotion REFUSED, rule retired as unmeasurable. Budget CLV since Jul 5 is -0.45pp (n=481 Kalshi / -0.37pp n=200 Odds API), so it fails budget_clv_pct_min a third straight time. But the composite no longer measures what it was written to measure: in Jul 2026 'budget' WAS MLB; it is now MLB+NFL+NBA+NHL, and the negative aggregate is carried by sports the Jul 4 package never touched (NBA -2.69pp n=23, NHL -0.48pp n=89) while MLB itself is -0.34pp and the promoted pattern -0.11pp. on_fail's prescribed demotion of dog_better_starter is explicitly NOT executed, and not on a judgement call: the promotion clears the KEEP line, not merely the demote line — 57-37 (60.6%) on budget picks, 132-83 (61.4%) over all 215 flagged, +3.5pp against market-implied. It is the best-performing component in the pool; demoting it because an aggregate that now includes three other sports went negative would be the opposite of what the evidence says. SUPERSEDED: src/state/clv_governor.py does per-(sport, market_type) CLV gating continuously and automatically — exactly this job, at the right granularity, without a hand-set annual threshold. Do not re-add an aggregate budget-CLV gate; it cannot distinguish the sports.

checkpoints.title: Candidate: MLB_HOME_ADVANTAGE 0.015 -> 0.0
checkpoints.rationale: Market prices home advantage; adding it double-counts (same mechanism as the refuted injury adjustment). Survived June split-half (+5.0/+4.2pp vs shipped) but is a second-generation tweak mined from June data — this out-of-sample window is its honest test.
checkpoints.resolution: FAILED out-of-sample Jul 19 (see health report): variant worse than live on Jul 5+ window. Discarded per on_fail.

checkpoints.title: Candidate: MLB_RUNLINE_SIGMA 3.5 -> 3.0
checkpoints.rationale: Empirical MLB final-margin SD ~3.1; 3.5 over-flattens run-line probabilities. Survived June split-half (+5.6/+7.2pp) but same second-generation caveat as ha_zero.
checkpoints.resolution: FAILED out-of-sample Jul 19 (see health report): variant worse than live on Jul 5+ window. Discarded per on_fail.

checkpoints.title: Pattern-concentrated card (bet the patterns, skip the rest)
checkpoints.rationale: No constants combo makes a forced full 5-pick MLB slate profitable at 4.5% friction; the profitable pockets are the promoted pattern and large edges. Budget = promoted picks + edges >= 0.08, variable card size. ⚠️ CORRECTED Jul 19: original window (2026-06-13) included the pattern's DISCOVERY data — the Jul 18 'PASS' (58.5%/+2.1%) was in-sample contamination; the July-only out-of-sample slice was 48.6%/-15.8% (n=37, worse than live). Window reset to Jul 5+, min_picks raised to 80, re-evaluate Aug 2. Lesson: a checkpoint's data window must NEVER include the data that generated the hypothesis.
checkpoints.on_pass: Propose to user as budget policy (display/watchlist unchanged): budget accepts only promoted picks and edges >= 0.08; skip thin days.
checkpoints.on_fail: Keep the current 5-pick card with the 0.05 floor.
checkpoints.resolution: RESOLVED Oct 29 2026 — clean FAIL, on_fail executed (no change). n=211 (>= min_picks 80) over 68 days of the corrected out-of-sample window, wr 54.5%, ROI -4.6% against pass_if_roi_gt 0.0. The Jul 18 'PASS' was in-sample contamination and the corrected window confirms it. Keeping the 5-pick card with the 0.05 floor. Question CLOSED — this was the last of the MLB full-game card-shape hypotheses, and it joins the Aug 4 verdict.

checkpoints.title: Candidate: promoted pattern picks bypass the 5% budget edge floor
checkpoints.rationale: Design tension surfaced Jul 10 (user-observed live case): SD Padres +1.5 was a promoted dog-with-better-starter pick at 4.8% edge - ranked 3rd on the MLB tab (confidence-first) but vetoed from the budget by BUDGET_MIN_EDGE=0.05; its replacement (Royals +1.5, 6.1% generic spread) lost while the Padres pick led. The promotion's qualification is the PATTERN, not the edge size - if the pattern validates at the package_health checkpoint, sub-floor promoted picks may be exactly the bets the floor should not veto. This variant lets promoted picks with any positive edge enter the budget.
checkpoints.on_pass: Ship: budget routing admits promoted (dog_better_starter) picks with edge > 0 regardless of BUDGET_MIN_EDGE (implement in main.py budget filter; stamp behavior into decision log features).
checkpoints.on_fail: Keep the floor absolute; promoted picks below 5% stay display-only.
checkpoints.resolution: FAILED out-of-sample Jul 19 (see health report): variant worse than live on Jul 5+ window. Discarded per on_fail.

checkpoints.title: FLIP TOTALS idea (Jun 14) — bet the opposite of the model's totals pick
checkpoints.rationale: Original idea: fade the model's totals picks (+5.3% ROI backtested pre-fix). Deferred because the Jun 13 source fix (league_avg_runs 4.5->4.35) could change the bias direction.
checkpoints.resolution: RESOLVED Jul 6 2026: the Jul 2 input-by-input analysis answered the deciding question — the source fix OVERSHOT. The model now has an UNDER bias (~99% of made totals are Unders, projected total avg 1.7 runs below the line, CLV still -2.1%). Flipping is NOT validated in either direction (unders still WIN 52.5% — they lose on price, not direction; and pre-fix flip evidence was for fading OVERS which barely exist now). Decision: totals stay CLV-gated out of the budget; the real fix is the run-expectation level (league_avg_runs / xFIP deflation / _TOTAL_MARKET_ANCHOR) — a candidate for a future registered checkpoint if totals are ever worth un-gating.

checkpoints.title: NBA constants re-audit with full logging infrastructure
checkpoints.rationale: NBA was the historical profit engine (+21.7% ROI in-season) but its constants have NEVER been audited with the decision-log infrastructure (no logged model inputs existed before Jun 13 2026 — NBA season ended Jun 13). When NBA returns (~late Oct), the decision log will capture full features from day one. After ~2-3 weeks of games: run the same reconstruction sweep MLB got Jul 3-4 (tools/analysis/backtest.py needs an NBA variant — reconstruct from NBA features), validate rating-edge weights, rest/B2B, injury handling (NBA injury adjustment is position-only — the MLB value-weighting fix was never ported), and credibility cap. Also verify the hot-streak question: was +21.7% real edge or variance? CLV data will now answer it. EXECUTION NOTE (Jul 15): run this audit with dynamic workflows + adversarial review (user pre-approved — parallel sweep segments, independent agent attacks the methodology for overfit/look-ahead/vig errors before conclusions are presented). Also suggest the user runs /code-review ultra on whatever package ships from it.

checkpoints.title: ERA-trap bonus: should it use ERA-FIP instead of ERA-xFIP?
checkpoints.rationale: FIP-blend hypothesis REFUTED Jul 5 (backing FIP-xFIP>1.0 starters is the BEST segment: 58.1% wr, +6.6% ROI, n=105 — never blend FIP into the quality score). Residual: within own-starter ERA-xFIP>1.0 picks, HR-driven gaps ran worse than sequencing-driven (52.3%/-4.4% vs 58.1%/+5.0%) at n=43 — re-test when both buckets reach ~100.
checkpoints.resolution: RESOLVED Oct 29 2026 — underpowered and now moot. Measured on 1172 made+settled MLB Moneyline decision-log rows since Jun 14, splitting own-starter ERA-xFIP>1.0 picks by whether FIP-xFIP>0.3 (HR-driven) or not (sequencing-driven): HR-driven 100-133 (42.9%, n=233), sequencing-driven 30-25 (54.5%, n=55), no-trap 402-422 (48.8%, n=824). Direction matches the Jul 5 observation, but min_n_per_bucket=100 is still unmet on the sequencing side and the 11.6pp gap is ~1.6 s.e. It will never be met: the MLB season is over, and the bucket only fills from MLB full-game picks. Moot regardless — MLB full-game was closed Aug 4 2026 (five independent tests), and a new constant keyed on this split is precisely the additive change that finding forbids. No action.

checkpoints.title: NFL warm-start (season cold-start prior) — early-season validation
checkpoints.rationale: Jul 2026 NFL audit found THREE compounding bugs that made the model unusable at season start: (1) ESPN standings nesting changed conf->division->teams to conf->teams, so _fetch_all_team_stats returned ZERO teams (every game cold-started even mid-season); (2) ESPN dropped avgPointsFor/Against, so season TOTALS were used as per-game (net ratings ~17x inflated → impossible favorites); (3) no prior-season carryover, so Week 1 rated every team net=0 and bet phantom underdogs against strong favorites (proven: Carolina +15% vs KC 78% market). All three FIXED Jul 24: robust entry collection, per-game division, warm-start blend (prior net regressed x0.67 toward mean, ramping out over 6 games via games_played weight). EVALUATE ~Oct 5 (after ~4 weeks / Weeks 1-4): are NFL budget picks' CLV >= 0 and win rate sane? Watch the warm_start_weight decision-log feature — do warm-start-active (early) picks under/over-perform? NFL is a BUDGET (real-money) sport, so if early CLV is negative the CLV governor auto-gates it; consider forcing watchlist-only or reduced confidence for Weeks 1-2 next season if the warm start proves insufficient.
checkpoints.resolution: RESOLVED Oct 29 2026 — SPLIT VERDICT: the CLV half passes, the win-rate half FAILS, and the failure is the larger finding. n=242 settled NFL picks since Sep 1 (29 of them budget). CLV >= 0: PASS. Kalshi CLV +0.05pp over the pool, +0.14pp on budget picks — NFL is in fact the only budget sport with positive CLV. Win rate sane: FAIL. NFL picks won 43.4% where the market implied 50.7% — -7.3pp against market, on n=242 (1 s.e. = 3.2pp, so ~2.3 s.e.). Budget picks -7.6pp. No other sport is close over the same window: MLB +0.6pp (n=2896), NBA +1.2pp (n=170), NHL -3.5pp (n=432). The model claimed 59.5% against a 43.4% outcome, a +16.1pp overclaim vs MLB's +7.0pp. The warm start is implicated but is not the whole story: Sep was -11.6pp and Oct -3.7pp, improving as the prior decays exactly as predicted — but October alone is still negative. NOT a broken input: NFL's raw |model-market| median is 10.9pp with the cap firing 33.7%, both in line with NBA (12.5pp / 47.8%) and NHL (11.8pp / 31.6%), so this is not the MLS xGF signature. Note the tension worth remembering: CLV said neutral while outcomes said -7pp, i.e. our fastest signal did not see this. ACTION REQUIRED is a money decision and belongs to the user — see the new checkpoint nfl_budget_probation.

checkpoints.title: First-5-innings suite — does it beat the market where full-game MLB failed?
checkpoints.rationale: Aug 4 2026: three independent tests proved the full-game MLB model has no exploitable edge (budget CLV -0.65% over n=212; features WORSEN out-of-sample log-loss; when we disagree with the market the market is right, worse the bigger our claimed edge). F5 is the one remaining hypothesis with a MECHANISTIC reason to work: (a) it is a bet on the STARTING PITCHERS ONLY — the model's deepest input (composite sp_score) — with the bullpen term (our weakest input) removed entirely; (b) F5/derivative markets are thinner and often algorithmically derived from the full-game line rather than independently priced; (c) unlike constants tuning, it has never been tested rather than repeatedly falsified. Built watchlist-only: markets 'F5 Moneyline'/'F5 Tie'/'F5 Spread'/'F5 Total' are in BUDGET_EXCLUDED_MARKETS, so they display + log + accrue CLV with ZERO money at risk. Calibration guarded by tests/test_f5.py (a first draft mis-scaled the pitcher weight and produced 15pp phantom edges; correct scaling is x5/9). Settlement uses the 5-inning linescore, never the final. || REVISED Aug 10 2026: F5 CLV is UNAVAILABLE and this checkpoint no longer uses it. The Odds API historical endpoint does not serve *_1st_5_innings at all (every wave returned 'Markets not supported by this endpoint'); the only sources that do were judged not worth the credits (per-event historical ~13.5k/mo; hourly pre-game sweep ~1.35k/mo). F5_CLV_ENABLED=False in closing_lines.py. Consequence: the fast skill signal is gone, so this is now a SLOW win/loss verdict and min_graded_picks rises 100 -> 400 with the evaluation pushed to Sep 14. Even 400 is a SCREEN, not proof: SE on win rate at n=400 is ~2.5pp, so only a large edge is detectable. That is why the both-halves requirement below is not optional — it is the only guard left against reading noise as skill. || Aug 25 2026 — CLV IS BACK FOR F5. Kalshi provides F5 closing lines free and BACKFILLABLE (settled markets retain 1-minute candles past our first F5 pick on Aug 4), stamped as kalshi_clv. The fast skill signal this checkpoint lost is therefore available again: ~50 graded picks per market gives a verdict that win/loss needs 500+ for. When evaluating, use kalshi_clv for F5 — it is self-consistent (Kalshi mid at pick vs Kalshi mid at close) and must NOT be compared against sportsbook-sourced clv on other markets.
checkpoints.on_pass: Requires ALL THREE, since CLV can no longer corroborate: (1) market_test.py shows F5 features improve out-of-sample log-loss vs market-price-only; (2) positive ROI at realistic vig in BOTH halves of a time split, not just overall; (3) n >= 400 graded picks. Only then remove F5 from BUDGET_EXCLUDED_MARKETS. If full-game MLB is still failing, propose the swap: F5 becomes the budget market, full-game drops to display-only.
checkpoints.on_fail: Keep F5 watchlist-only or retire it. If F5 ALSO shows no edge, that is strong evidence the limit is our public-data inputs rather than the market chosen — at which point the honest recommendation is to stop betting MLB in any form and let NFL/Liga MX be judged on their own. NOTE: without CLV, a fail here is weaker evidence than the Aug 4 full-game verdict was; say so rather than overclaiming.
checkpoints.resolution: FAIL — do NOT graduate F5 to budget. n=769 settled picks (threshold was 400), 2026-08-08..2026-09-18. ROI at the no-vig mid is +0.78%, which is the number that made F5 look alive; at the MEASURED execution cost it is not. Ask costs +0.72pp over our no-vig price (measured on 158 execution-log rows, not assumed), taking ROI to -0.62%, and the /bin/zsh.02 per-contract fee takes it to -4.48% — on a ~/bin/zsh.50 contract that fee alone is ~4% of stake, and it is the DOMINANT cost, larger than crossing the spread. || DECISIVE: the time split fails outright, +0.98% first half vs -9.95% second half, so there is no stable edge to size into. Kalshi CLV is flat to negative (F5 Spread -0.18% n=443, F5 Total -0.07% n=283); only F5 Moneyline is positive (+0.20%) on n=43, too small to mean anything. || The original F5 thesis was mechanistic and reasonable: bet the starting pitchers (our deepest input) with the bullpen (our weakest) removed, in a thinner market. The thesis is not refuted by noise here — it is refuted by 769 picks and a failed time split. F5 stays watchlist-only and keeps logging; revisit ONLY with a new mechanism, never by rerunning this same test on more of the same data.

checkpoints.title: One budget bet per game — does removing same-game doubles help?
checkpoints.rationale: Shipped Aug 10 2026 after the user spotted the card holding 'Athletics +1.5' AND 'Rays ML' on the same game — near-opposite bets that both win only if the Rays win by exactly 1, i.e. a hedge paying vig twice. The old dedup keyed on (game, team/direction), so it caught a duplicate of the SAME bet but never two different MARKETS on one game. MAX_BUDGET_BETS_PER_GAME=1 keeps the best-ranked pick and gives the freed slot to the next game; display pools are unchanged. || HONESTY ON THE BACKTEST: it shows +2.51pp ROI (-7.71 -> -5.20) with both halves of a time split agreeing almost exactly (+2.49 / +2.52) — but that agreement is MECHANICAL, not independent confirmation. The rule only changes 19 of 252 picks: dropped went 7-12 (-6.80u), replacements went 10-9 (-0.49u). n=19 is far too small to call, and the halves share that same small set. Treat the ROI gain as NOT ESTABLISHED. Note also that CLV moved the WRONG way (0.57% -> 0.38%), so our best signal does not corroborate the outcome gain. || SHIPPED ANYWAY on STRUCTURAL grounds, which is the real justification and does not depend on the data: two picks on one game are correlated by construction, concentrate risk on a single outcome, and in the opposing case cap the upside while paying vig twice. This is the subtractive kind of change that has historically worked for us, not the additive kind that has repeatedly failed.
checkpoints.on_pass: If ROI on the post-ship window is >= the pre-ship baseline and no same-game pair has appeared on a card, keep the rule.
checkpoints.on_fail: Do NOT revert on ROI alone — the structural argument stands independent of the outcome data, and n will still be small. Revert only if the rule is demonstrably costing slots (e.g. cards routinely shipping fewer than MAX_SINGLE_BETS picks).
checkpoints.open_gap: RESOLVED Aug 10 2026 (same session, user said extend it): _parlay_valid now blocks ALL same-game leg pairs, not just ML+Spread. Spread+Total and ML+Total on one game were being priced as if independent. Impact on live behaviour is near zero — 33 of the 35 historical same-game parlays predate June 2026 and the one July case was the duplicate-leg bug — so this is a safety rail, not a behaviour change. Could not be measured: none of the 35 reconstruct against the shadow log (their legs predate reliable logging), so there is NO outcome evidence either way. Shipped on the same structural grounds as the singles rule. Revisit only with a real correlation model, never by relaxing the rule.
checkpoints.resolution: RESOLVED Oct 29 2026 — PASS, rule kept. Verified on the shipped money cards, not just the logs: of 180 picks files with a singles card, 20 contained a same-game pair and ALL 20 predate the rule, the last being 2026-08-10 (the 'Tampa Bay Rays @ Athletics' case that triggered it). Zero since, across 349 budget game-days. Not costing slots: budget cards average 4.53 picks post-ship vs 4.47 pre-ship, with 58 of 77 at the full 5 — the short cards are thin days, not the rule. Outcome data, as predicted, establishes nothing: -0.9pp vs market post-ship (n=343) against -1.1pp pre-ship (n=140), CLV -0.42pp vs -0.52pp. Both move the right way, both well inside noise. The rule stands on the structural argument, which never depended on this data. FOUND AND FIXED while checking this: the shadow log's `displayed_in_top` flag was built for watchlist sports WITHOUT _one_per_game or _pwa_display_eligible, while the actual tile applies both — so the log marked picks as displayed that no tile ever showed (51 phantom same-game pairs Aug 11 - Oct 28, every one watchlist). The money card was never affected. Budget and watchlist now share one definition in main.py.

checkpoints.title: Does buying at the BID instead of the ask make MLB break even?
checkpoints.rationale: Aug 24 2026: measured that we pay ask + $0.02 fees on every bet. On a coin-flip contract that is ~2pp over fair value, and our measured edge is ~0 (budget CLV -0.41%), so purchase price is most of the -3.2pp shortfall, not the model. Robinhood's sports contracts ARE Kalshi and the app shows Kalshi's raw ask (verified to the cent: a Rays ML quoted 0.56 in-app vs 0.56 on the API). Kalshi's data API is public and free. || WHAT DIED HERE: the cross-venue arbitrage idea. On liquid full-game markets Kalshi tracks the sharp consensus within 0.5-1.0pp, far inside the 2.5pp hurdle -- the 'prediction markets misprice vs sharp books' gap is NOT present in MLB moneylines/run lines. The only 3.5pp gap found was in a thin F5 total, and its edge pointed at the OPPOSITE side from our model's pick. || WHAT IS BEING TESTED NOW: resting at the bid instead of taking the ask saves the spread (1c typical, 2c occasionally; ~1.25pp average on the Aug 24 card). But fills are ADVERSELY SELECTED -- a resting order is hit preferentially when the price is about to move against you -- so the quoted spread OVERSTATES the real saving. The user confirms fills are inconsistent in practice. Crucially, for a bettor with ~0 edge an UNFILLED order costs nothing: we skip a zero-EV bet rather than forgo profit. So 'post at bid, never chase' is close to free for us specifically.
checkpoints.on_pass: If average clv_if_bid on picks that WOULD have filled is > 0 after fees, AND it holds in both halves of a time split, AND fill rate is high enough to keep a usable card: adopt 'post at bid, skip if unfilled' as policy and surface the bid price on every card.
checkpoints.on_fail: If even at the bid we are underwater, execution is not the answer and the MLB pause decision returns with one fewer escape route. Do NOT respond by hunting new model constants -- that question was closed Aug 4.
checkpoints.measurement: python3 -m tools.analysis.execution_report. Fill detection replays Kalshi candlesticks and asks whether the market traded at or below our bid; it IGNORES QUEUE POSITION, so reported fill rate is an OPTIMISTIC UPPER BOUND. Adverse selection = clv_if_bid on filled picks minus clv_if_bid on all picks; a negative number is the real cost of waiting.
checkpoints.resolution: RESOLVED Oct 29 2026 — FAIL. n=201 settled MLB picks (>= min 150), Aug 27 - Oct 28. CLV if we always took the ask -2.59pp; if we always got the bid -1.54pp; the spread is worth +1.05pp. Fill rate at the bid 96% (193/201) — an OPTIMISTIC upper bound, it ignores queue position. Adverse selection is only -0.02pp, so waiting is nearly free, which was the hypothesis and it held. It does not matter: even at the bid we are -1.55pp after $0.02 fees, so the saving (+1.05pp) is smaller than the shortfall (-2.59pp). By market: Spread -1.78pp at bid (n=144), Moneyline -0.93pp (n=57). Both still negative, so the time-split condition in on_pass is moot. Execution is NOT the answer; per on_fail, do not respond by hunting model constants.

checkpoints.title: Can Kalshi CLV replace Odds API CLV (and cut ~54% of credits)?
checkpoints.rationale: Odds API historical CLV is ~190 of ~353 daily credits (~54%). Kalshi's data is free, public, keyless, retains settled markets with 1-minute candlestick history, and covers every registry sport except IPL. It also provides F5 closing lines, which the Odds API cannot serve AT ANY PRICE. || BUILT ADDITIVE ON PURPOSE: writes kalshi_* fields only. `clv` and `market_prob_at_close` — which calibration and the CLV governor read — are untouched, verified by a byte-hash of those fields before/after (3752 rows, hash unchanged) plus a governor recompute that reproduced all 19 market rows identically. || ⛔ DO NOT SWITCH YET. Correlation FELL as the sample grew: 0.786 at n=27, 0.453 at n=262, and 0.253 at n=1064 (the full backfilled set, Jul 5 onward). The small-sample figure was noise; the large-sample figure is the answer. The two measure the same idea in different venues and are NOT interchangeable on this evidence. CLV values are tiny (mean -0.23pp, mean |difference| 0.87pp), so noise attenuates correlation, but that is a reason for more data, not for switching. || RESULT Aug 25: correlation 0.253 on 1064 paired rows, mean |difference| 1.25pp against CLV values averaging -0.39pp / -0.08pp. The difference is LARGER than the signal. These are NOT interchangeable and the credit saving is OFF THE TABLE until something changes. What was gained anyway: 312 F5 rows now carry CLV (183 Spread + 112 Total + 17 Moneyline) where the Odds API can serve none, and MLB full-game Kalshi coverage now MATCHES the Odds API (468 vs 465 Moneyline, 444 vs 434 Spread) — so F5 gets its fast signal back before Sep 14. || ⚠️ TEST CORRECTED Aug 25 (user's reframe, and they were right). The original gate was correlation BETWEEN the two sources — i.e. 'does Kalshi reproduce the sportsbook number?' That is the wrong question. CLV is only worth anything if it PREDICTS RESULTS, so the test is which source better separates our winners from losers ON THE SAME ROWS. A source can correlate poorly with the other and still be the better signal — and Kalshi has the stronger claim on principle, being the book we actually trade in. || MEASURED (n=1061 settled paired rows): Odds API r=+0.0205, CLV>0 wins 55.3% vs 51.7% (gap +3.6pp). Kalshi r=+0.0327, CLV>0 wins 56.2% vs 51.6% (gap +4.7pp). Kalshi is the STRONGER predictor on both measures — but 1 s.e. on a correlation at this n is ~0.031, so the difference is INSIDE noise. The honest reading is a TIE, and 'at least as good' is all that is needed to justify a free source. || ⛔ THE REAL BLOCKER IS HISTORY DEPTH, not quality: Kalshi retains settled markets only back to 2026-06-18, while the shadow log starts in April. Switching truncates the CLV governor's window to mid-June onward, shrinking the samples its gates fire on (e.g. MLB Total n=593 today). That is the thing to solve before switching, and no amount of waiting fixes it — Kalshi's retention window MOVES FORWARD, so the pre-June history is permanently unreachable.
checkpoints.on_pass: Switch only if ALL hold: (1) Kalshi predictive r >= Odds API r on >= 800 settled paired rows; (2) Kalshi coverage >= Odds API coverage per market; (3) a decision is made about the governor's truncated window — either accept the shorter history explicitly, or run both sources with the governor still reading the Odds API series until Kalshi's own window is long enough to gate on. Do NOT switch silently mid-series: the seam is invisible in the panels and the governor would gate on a mixed-venue average.
checkpoints.on_fail: Keep both. F5 CLV via Kalshi is a pure gain regardless — it is the only source that exists for those markets — and it costs nothing to keep capturing in parallel.
checkpoints.open_gap: Watchlist sports (WNBA/MLS/WC/LIGAMX) get NO Kalshi CLV: kalshi.TEAM_TO_KALSHI maps MLB teams only, so those entries are skipped — deliberately WITHOUT burning a retry attempt, so they light up the moment team maps are added. Their Kalshi series exist and were verified present. LIGAMX has no Odds API CLV either (0 rows), so it is currently blind.
checkpoints.resolution: RESOLVED Oct 29 2026 — the switch already happened, correctly, and events closed the question. The paid Odds API was cancelled Oct 27 2026 and its key is dead (401), so the >= 800 paired rows this gate asked for will never accrue: 595 is the final number and it is frozen. What the evidence says on those 595 settled paired rows: Kalshi is the stronger predictor on both measures (r=+0.0668 vs +0.0153; CLV>0 wins 52.0% vs 48.3%, gap +3.6pp, against the Odds API's +0.0pp gap) — though 1 s.e. is ~0.041, so read it as a tie, which is all 'at least as good' required. Coverage is decisive rather than marginal: 4089 rows vs 595 overall (96% vs 14%), and Kalshi >= Odds API in EVERY market, with 13 markets (all F5, CFB, NFL, NHL, NBA, LIGAMX) that the Odds API cannot serve at any price. on_pass condition (3) is satisfied by the second of its two options, already implemented: clv_governor.effective_clv() prefers kalshi_clv and FALLS BACK to the sportsbook clv, so the pre-Jun-18 history the governor gates on is preserved rather than truncated, and there is no invisible mid-series seam. CLV_PREFER_KALSHI=True is the switch; it is on.

checkpoints.title: College football Elo-margin model — any signal at all?
checkpoints.rationale: Added as a WATCHLIST sport Sep 1 2026. Modelled as a POINT MARGIN, not probabilities: ~134 FBS teams play ~12 games each with huge talent dispersion, so a power rating that converts to a spread is the right shape and per-game stat aggregation never gets the sample it needs. margin = elo_gap/25 + 2.6 home; P(cover) = Phi((margin+line)/16.5). || WHY IT MIGHT WORK WHERE MLB DID NOT: far more games, far less sharp attention on small matchups, and much wider dispersion to model. || WHY IT PROBABLY WILL NOT: the inputs are public, which is exactly what failed everywhere else. Elo from public results is not privileged data. || ⛔ LIQUIDITY CEILING, measured Aug 29 2026: Kalshi CFB moneyline median spread is 8 CENTS (MLB is 1), and the spread/total books show median open interest of ZERO with 16-18c spreads. Only marquee games have real depth. So even a working model is actionable on a handful of games a week — this exists to answer 'is there signal', NOT 'can we bet it'. Do not propose graduating CFB to budget on model results alone; the books have to be there too. || ⚠️ FIRST SLATE WAS GARBAGE — window restarted Sep 4. On Sep 3 the model produced 5 picks at EXACTLY +8.0% edge, the credibility cap value, on +26.5 to +42.5 underdogs it believed were near-even. Cause: week-1 Elo spanned only 372 points (max expressible margin 14.9) while the lines reached 42.5 — the model could not REPRESENT the game, and the cap clamped every pick to its ceiling. Measured against the market's own lines, the implied conversion was ~3 Elo per point versus our constant of 25, i.e. ratings compressed ~8x. FCS teams were also being rated (236 teams vs ~134 FBS; North Dakota State rated 2nd overall). || A CAP THAT FIRES ON 100% OF PICKS IS A SYMPTOM, NOT A SAFETY NET — that is the F5 calibration trap again, caught before shipping there and not caught here. Gate added: skip when our projected margin disagrees with the market line by more than CFB_MAX_MARGIN_DISAGREE (10 pts), plus a CFB_MIN_RATED_GAMES floor. Replaying Sep 3 through the gate suppresses all 7 games. Pre-Sep-4 CFB rows in the shadow/decision logs come from the broken model and MUST be excluded from any evaluation.
checkpoints.on_pass: If Kalshi CLV >= 0 over >= 250 graded picks AND positive in both halves of a time split: report it, then check per-game liquidity BEFORE proposing any budget role. A signal in unbettable markets is a finding, not an edge.
checkpoints.on_fail: Retire or keep as a display curiosity. A CFB failure alongside MLB's would be further evidence the limit is our public-data inputs rather than the sport chosen — which is the same conclusion the F5 checkpoint is testing.
checkpoints.open_gap: Totals are deliberately NOT modelled (need a pace x efficiency model, and they are the worst-priced CFB market on Kalshi). SP+ deferred by user decision: it is famous and public, so the market already prices it — worth considering only as a BASELINE to compare our rating against, never as the model itself. || ⛔ THE RATINGS ARE STILL NOT FIT FOR PURPOSE. The gate stops bad picks but does not make good ones: with a 372-point Elo range the model can only express margins up to ~15 points, so it will simply stay silent on most of the slate. Fixing this needs a genuinely wider rating spread (more seasons replayed, a margin-based rating rather than win/loss Elo, or seeding from preseason ratings) — NOT retuning CFB_ELO_TO_POINTS, which would only rescale a compressed range into differently-wrong numbers.

checkpoints.title: CFB credibility cap can finally self-tune — does it widen or hold?
checkpoints.rationale: Found Sep 11 2026 while checking why two Kansas picks both carried an edge of exactly 0.08000: analyze_cfb_game called _apply_credibility_cap_dispatched(...)[0], taking the capped probability and DISCARDING [1], the fired flag. _stamp_recs_calibration only fills that flag in when model_prob_raw is still None, and CFB always sets it — so credibility_cap_fired was False on every CFB pick ever produced, including ones where the cap clipped a 12.6pp raw edge down to 8.0pp. || WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND DISPLAY: cap_state.evaluate_and_adjust_caps reads ONLY cap-fired rows to run its raw_mae-vs-capped_mae counterfactual. With zero rows ever flagged, the CFB cap was structurally unable to self-tune — it would have sat at 0.08 forever while every other sport adapted. The cap firing on BOTH picks of a slate is the same symptom flagged Sep 4: a cap that fires on ~100% of picks is a model-disagreement signal, not a safety net. || WHAT TO CHECK: with >=60 recorded firings, does the counterfactual widen the cap (model adds signal past 8pp), tighten it (drift is noise), or hold? A cap still firing on a majority of CFB picks at evaluation time means the SRS margin and the market disagree systematically, and cfb_validation is the checkpoint that matters.

checkpoints.title: Projected score now derived from the model probability — does the card still read right?
checkpoints.rationale: User caught the Sep 17 NFL card picking Detroit while projecting Buffalo by 1. The projected score was built from season scoring averages alone while the win probability came from team strength + home field + injuries + rest + caps, so the two were free to disagree. Measured across live cards: NFL mean 6.2 pts off, worst 27.7 with the SIGN FLIPPED (Sep 10 SF@LAR projected LAR by 24 while the model believed SF by 3.7); WNBA mean 4.9. || CHANGE: the TOTAL still comes from scoring data, the MARGIN now comes from the final post-cap probability (_score_from_prob), so they agree by construction in NFL/NBA/NHL/WNBA. CFB already did this. DISPLAY ONLY — no probability, edge, or stake changes. || WHAT TO CHECK: that projected scores now look sane against actual results (the margin is a median-ish expectation, not a point forecast), and that the value-underdog note reads clearly on cards where we back a side the model expects to lose. If projected totals now look systematically off, the TOTAL formula is the suspect, not the split.

checkpoints.title: Totals keep the vig — fix once NHL Total has enough CLV to gate itself
checkpoints.rationale: Found Oct 5 2026 while comparing Kalshi and Odds API pricing. _consensus_probs in odds_client.py de-vigs h2h and spreads per book but NOT totals: moneyline sides sum to exactly 1.0000 while totals sides sum to 1.046-1.063 in EVERY sport. Each totals side is inflated ~2.3pp, so edge = model - market is understated by the same amount and totals under-rank against ML/spread in slot selection. || NOT FIXED ON PURPOSE (user decision): de-vigging makes 46% more totals candidates clear the edge floor (674 -> 984 measured on the decision log), and totals are our worst market. MLB Total (-0.70%), MLS Total (-1.39%), NBA Total (-2.19%) and WC Total (-2.04%) are already CLV-gated out of the budget. The ungated ones are NFL Total (+0.00%, n=38) and NHL Total (-1.81%, n=11, phase 0). So the arithmetic error is currently PROTECTIVE and fixing it would add real-money exposure precisely where CLV is weakest. || TRIGGER: NHL Total reaching n>=30 lets the governor decide for itself (phase 1). At that point fix the de-vig so exposure is controlled by the gates rather than by a bug, and INVERT tests/test_price_compare.py::test_totals_sides_do_NOT_sum_to_one. || NOTE CLV is unaffected by this bug: it is a difference of two market probs, so a constant overround cancels. The existing totals CLV verdicts stand.

checkpoints.title: NBA warm start + preseason exclusion — did the opening weeks behave?
checkpoints.rationale: Asked ahead of the opener. TWO defects, both would have shipped. (1) The standings call omitted seasontype and ESPN defaults to the league's current phase — PRESEASON before opening night. Verified live: default gave Atlanta 0W-1L, seasontype=2 gave 0W-0L. One preseason game produced net ratings of -34..+34 (sd 13.7) vs a real NBA spread of -12..+11 (sd 6.1), and a simulated matchup yielded a +15.0% moneyline edge with the credibility cap FIRING — the CFB first-slate signature. (2) NBA had no warm start, unlike NFL, so with preseason excluded every team sits at the 110/110 default and EVERY matchup prices identically at 58% — no signal at all. Fixing one alone leaves garbage or flatness. || FIX: seasontype=2 on the standings call, games_played captured, and _apply_warm_start blending last season regressed by NBA_PRIOR_REGRESSION=0.60 over a 15-game ramp. The 0.60 is MEASURED: season-over-season net-rating slope across four pairs (2022->23..2025->26) was 0.445/0.779/0.633/0.543, mean 0.600, with a stable r of 0.52-0.59. NBA regresses slightly MORE than NFL (0.67), the opposite of what roster stability suggests — hence measuring. The 15-game ramp outlasts the ~8-game crossover where the current sample (se=12/sqrt(n)) beats the prior residual (~5.0). || RESULT: model win-prob spread 36-76%, sd 8.4pp, 9% outside 30-70% — a believable NBA distribution, versus flat-58% without the warm start. || WHAT TO CHECK: edge DISTRIBUTION on the first two weeks. If most picks sit at the credibility cap, the model is overconfident again and the ramp or regression needs work — a cap firing on most picks is a symptom, not a safety net. Also confirm warm_start_weight falls from 0.0 toward 1.0 as games accrue, and that it reaches 1.0 by ~mid-November.
checkpoints.evidence: Oct 29 2026 — concrete early evidence, surfaced by the new model-sanity detector rather than by anyone looking. NBA Total picks are 67 'under' to 3 'over' (63/63 one-sided in the last 14 days), the credibility cap fires on 71% of them, and the model's expected_total has a median of 226.3 against a market line median of 232.5 — systematically 6.2 POINTS LOW across the whole slate. That is why every pick is an Under: it is one bias, not 63 opinions. Consistent with a cold-start scoring baseline: the season is ~1 week old, so team scoring rates come off 3-5 games. The CLV governor had ALREADY gated NBA Total independently (avg -3.18%, n=68), so no money is flowing there — two mechanisms agreeing, which is the system behaving as intended. Deliberately NOT fixed now: adjusting a scoring baseline one week into a season, on 144 decision rows, is how you fit to noise. Re-measure at the Dec 1 date with ~6 weeks of real games. If expected_total is STILL ~6 points below the market line then, it is not a cold start and the scoring model's league baseline is wrong.
checkpoints.measured_oct30: MEASURED Oct 30 2026 against 58 ACTUAL final scores (this season only; one stale June playoff row dropped). The symptom was 'NBA totals are 6 points low'. That framing was wrong — it compared the model to the MARKET, and the market is the thing that is off: actual mean total 227.3 | model (blended) 225.9 | market line 232.0. So the MODEL is ~2.0pp low and the BOOK is ~4.2 points high (median +4.5). The model's mean absolute error is LOWER than the market's — 14.41 vs 14.72 — i.e. it is the most accurate of the three, and the 73/73 one-sided Unders reflect a real early-season market bias rather than a broken input. ⚠️ EVERY CORRECTION TESTED MADE IT WORSE, which is why nothing was changed. Eight variants on 58 games: shipped blended MAE 14.73 (best), market line 15.03, raw-as-shipped 15.78, raw+injury restored 15.52 (bias improves to +0.52 but MAE degrades), raw+injury*0.5 15.40, raw+injury with the 0.4 anchor 15.10, raw+injury+B2B restored 15.18. The injury subtraction is ALSO uncorrelated with the error (r=+0.049), so it is not the mechanism — it is close to a constant offset, and removing it fixes the average while worsening individual games. Two errors are cancelling (raw over-subtracts ~5.4pts, the 40% market anchor pulls it back), which is ugly but empirically the best combination available. ⚠️ AND THE MARKET BIAS IS NOT YET REAL EITHER: z=+1.75, and a 4.7-point bias needs ~61 games at 2 s.e. while we have 58. The two halves of a time split disagree badly (+7.64 then +1.87), and single days swing from -11.5 to +36.5. Nothing here supports a constant change. The one-sided finding is ACKNOWLEDGED in src/state/model_sanity.py until this checkpoint's date, so it stays printed but stops alerting. RE-MEASURE at Dec 1 with ~6 weeks of games: if the model still beats the market's MAE, there is nothing to fix and the Under lean is a feature.

checkpoints.title: Kalshi replaces the Odds API as the price source for every budget sport

rules.pass: Kalshi-priced picks show CLV >= the Odds-API-priced baseline of -0.65% (MLB budget, n=212) AND the daily recommendation count stays within 50-150% of the 14-day Odds-API average AND no sport logs a fell_back rate above 20%.
rules.fail: Any budget sport systematically unpriceable (fell_back > 20% of its slates), or edges inflate (median budget edge rises above the Odds-API median by more than 2 points), or CLV degrades below -2%.

checkpoints.rationale: The user is cancelling the paid Odds API subscription, so this is a forced migration, not an optimisation — the checkpoint exists to catch harm, not to decide whether to switch. Measured before shipping: Kalshi-derived edges are MORE conservative than Odds-API ones (NBA median +7.8% vs +10.2%, NHL +8.7% vs +10.5%), because Kalshi's bid/ask midpoint on a two-sided book carries less overround slack than a multi-book no-vig consensus. That direction is the safe one — fewer, smaller edges rather than inflated ones. Kalshi IS Robinhood's book, so prices now come from the venue we actually trade in: open and close are finally measured at the same venue, which removes the venue-difference contamination the CLV rule warns about. || RISKS: (1) Discovery, not pricing, is the weak point — Kalshi can only build a slate for a sport with a verified static team map, so CFB/IPL/WC still need the free-tier Odds API key. (2) Untraded contracts quote 2c/98c and a naive midpoint reads as a 50% probability; MAX_SPREAD_CENTS=10 rejects those (caught live on MLS totals, which produced 'Over 0.5 goals at 50%'). (3) An empty Kalshi slate is ambiguous, so _espn_game_count cross-checks before warning — an alert that fires every quiet day is one the reader stops reading. (4) Player props went DARK but are NOT unavailable — the shipped claim that Kalshi has no player markets was WRONG, corrected same-day on live data: all eleven modelled markets exist (KXNBAPTS/REB/AST/STL/BLK/3PT, KXMLBKS/HIT/TB/HR/HRR), two-sided, 75% of 734 NBA contracts quoted inside the 10c filter. They are merely not wired to Kalshi yet and have never carried money (zero rows in the shadow log and every picks file). || REVERSIBLE WITHOUT A DEPLOY: PRICE_SOURCE=oddsapi forces the old path for every sport while a free-tier key exists.

checkpoints.title: Player props rebuilt on Kalshi's ladder + small-sample shrink

rules.pass: Prop CLV >= 0 over >=60 graded NBA props AND the median displayed prop edge sits below +8% (a median near the +15% credibility cap means the model is disagreeing with a liquid market systematically, which is the known failure signature, not signal).
rules.fail: Prop CLV < 0, or the median edge stays above +10%, or projections remain one-directional (>80% above the market). ANY of these means props stay display-and-log only and must NOT be routed to money.

checkpoints.rationale: Props were rewired from the cancelled Odds API onto Kalshi's binary ladder, treating the ladder as the native market rather than translating it into a sportsbook Over/Under: every rung is priced and the rung nearest 50% per (player, market) reaches the analyzer. A rung at N is P(stat>=N), passed as line N-0.5, which is the continuity correction and is EXACT for the Poisson markets. Verified live Oct 27: 734 NBA contracts across 4 games, 543 priced, 174 rungs across 45 players. || THE REASON THIS NEEDS A CHECKPOINT: the first working run produced 50 picks with a MEDIAN edge of +14.0%, maxing at the +15% credibility cap, with 48 of 54 projections ABOVE the market. Diagnosed, not guessed: median games played was ONE (season six days old) AND the Tier-1 stats source is ESPN's TOP-25 LEADERBOARD, so a thin sample was also a selected one — we were reading a player's single outlying game as his average (Camara 18.4 projected vs a 9.5 line; LaVine 28.3 vs 19.5). This is the team-side nba_warm_start defect, never fixed for players. || WORSE, AND THE REAL FIND: ESPN returns NO games-played count for prop players at all — all 43 came back 0 once the two defaults were removed. Those defaults were fabrications (leaders tier defaulted to 1, _BLANK_STATS to 40), so the props model had NEVER known how many games its averages covered. Sample size now comes from the TEAM's games_played, which is real and bounds the player's. || FIX: shrink_projection pulls the projection toward the MARKET's own implied mean with weight n/(n+12) and refuses to project below 4 games. Shrinking toward the market, not a league average, is deliberate — the market already prices minutes, role and injury risk, which a season average cannot see. Measured after: at 4 games median edge +3.9%, at 25 games +10.2%, at 60 games +12.3%. || ⚠️ THE RESIDUAL IS THE OPEN QUESTION: even at a full 60-game sample the median edge is +12.3% and still one-directional. That is NOT a sample-size artefact and it is the same shape as the MLB full-game result (our error grows with our claimed edge). Props carry zero money today (verified: no prop rows in any shadow-log shard or picks file) and MUST stay that way until market_test.py is run on prop features. || KNOWN GAP, not Kalshi's fault: MLB props stamp and enrich correctly (venue + probable pitcher resolve) but get_batter_props_stats returns EMPTY for correct names and team ids, so zero MLB props are produced. Likely regular-season stat endpoints being empty in the postseason. Low priority: the season ends within days and MLB full-game is a closed question.
checkpoints.known_gap_resolved: RESOLVED Oct 29 2026, and the diagnosis recorded above was WRONG. MLB props produced zero picks because get_batter_props_stats omitted `playerPool=ALL`, not because postseason endpoints are empty. The StatsAPI default is QUALIFIED (batting-title eligibility, ~3.1 PA per team game), so the call returned a median of 5 batters per team instead of 27 — 130 of 830 across all 30 teams, 16%. Kalshi lists props for ~2 dozen batters a game, almost none of them among those 5, so every lookup came back empty. This would have failed identically in June; it was never seasonal. ⚠️ THE SAME FLAG WAS MISSING FROM TWO MORE HITTING CALLS, and one of them touches real money: get_injury_value_mults scales injury impact by a player's offensive value, and QUALIFIED selects precisely for players who have NOT missed time — so it could only ever resolve healthy everyday regulars and every other injured hitter fell through to the caller's 1.0 default, i.e. the position-only behaviour the feature was written to replace. It has been close to inert since it shipped. get_team_batting_leaders was the third. All three fixed; after, 21 of 25 Yankees batters resolve (the 4 misses are under min_pa=30, which is correct) and injury value_mults span 0.36-2.91 with a median of 0.77 where they were previously almost all defaulted. ⚠️ THE LESSON: get_bullpen_stats has carried this flag AND a comment saying it is required since it was written. The fix was known and was applied to exactly one of four call sites. Pinned by tests/test_mlb_stats_player_pool.py, which walks the AST for every _get("/stats") call rather than checking the one function that broke. NOT verified end-to-end: the MLB season is over and all five Kalshi prop series return 0 open markets, so the stats half is proven on live data and the slate half cannot be until spring.

checkpoints.title: Kalshi spread sign was always 'home favoured' — inverted whenever the away team was favoured
checkpoints.resolution: FIXED same day, before the games started. `_best_spread` decided fav_is_home by comparing a rung's ticker suffix against the first three characters of THAT SAME SUFFIX (`"SAS14".startswith("SAS")`), so the test was unconditionally True and every spread was signed as if the home team were favoured — correct by luck when home was the favourite, inverted otherwise. Root cause of the wrong comparison: `_team_token()` returns a DISPLAY token ("San Antonio") while spread tickers carry an ABBREVIATION ("SAS"), so the two can never match and a bridging helper was written that silently compared the suffix to itself. Fixed by passing the home team's real ticker abbreviation, taken from the home moneyline market whose home/away resolution was already correct via ticker order — no second map to drift. Verified on the live Oct 28 slate: 17/17 games now agree between moneyline and spread on who is favoured; 9 of those 17 (every game with an away favourite) had been inverted. Measured effect on the same slate: NBA median edge fell from cap-pinned ~15% to +6.8%, spread picks on the '+' side went from 8/8 to 7/15, credibility cap firing fell from 70% to 37%, and NBA raw |model-market| fell from 17.2pp to 12.1pp — identical to the 12.2pp pre-switch baseline, which retires the suspicion that Kalshi pricing had inflated edges. NHL improved to 6.5pp from 10.2pp pre-switch, as predicted before the switch shipped. Regression tests in tests/test_kalshi_pricing.py::TestSpreadOrientation assert the invariant directly (moneyline and spread must agree on the favourite) rather than eyeballing a line.

rules.pass: moneyline and spread agree on the favourite for every discovered game

checkpoints.rationale: ⚠️ COST: real money was staked on inverted lines before this was caught — two NHL spreads and one MLB spread, $3.28 of the day's $5.50. The bug was invisible in the diff and invisible in the test suite; it was caught only by reading the live card, noticing 'San Antonio +12.5' for a team that was a 13-point favourite, and pulling that game's actual Kalshi ladder. This is the third time the 'verify on live data, not by reading code' rule has paid for itself, and the second home/away inversion on the Kalshi path after the soccer ticker-order bug — both silently wrong rather than absent. LESSON NOW ENCODED AS A TEST: when two markets in one game dict imply the same fact (who is favoured), assert that they agree. That single invariant would have caught this on day one.

checkpoints.title: Kalshi has no start-time field — commence_time was the settlement moment, ~3h late

rules.pass: commence_time matches ESPN tip-off for every discovered game

checkpoints.resolution: FIXED same day. `discover()` used Kalshi's `occurrence_datetime`, which equals `expected_expiration_time` — the expected SETTLEMENT moment, ~3h after tip for an NBA game. Verified: LAL@LAC on 2026-10-28 read 05:30Z when ESPN (authoritative) had 02:30Z. Corrected inside `stamp_game_types`, which already matched ESPN events to game dicts by team name within a 6h window, so no extra API calls: ESPN's `date` now overwrites commence_time when they differ by more than 10 minutes, logged with the worst drift. No-op on the Odds API path, which carries a real start time. Two further bugs surfaced while fixing it, both silent: (1) `_team_match` could not match ESPN's own displayName "LA Clippers" to our "Los Angeles Clippers" — token overlap gives one shared token against a two-token city difference — so LAL@LAC was the ONE game of twelve left uncorrected and the one game never stamped with a season type; fixed by routing both sides through `team_names.expand_city()`, the module that exists for exactly this. (2) `_ESPN_PATHS` was a hardcoded literal missing ligamx, wc and cfb, so those sports got neither a season type nor a time correction; it is now DERIVED from the settlement maps. After: 12/12 NBA, 4/4 NHL, 1/1 MLB, 14/14 MLS and 1/1 LigaMX corrected, worst drift 3.0h, and Liga MX moved from 11:00 PM to its real 8:00 PM.
checkpoints.rationale: ⚠️ NOT a cosmetic bug. commence_time drives the shadow log's GAME LOCK and the Kalshi CLV closing sample, so a 3h-late timestamp would have left picks editable deep into a game and sampled the 'close' AFTER the market had already resolved to 0 or 1 — silently corrupting the primary skill metric from its first Kalshi night. Caught because the user read the card and noticed a 10:30 PM tip for a game they knew was at 7:30 PM. Model-facing data should be checked against the authoritative feed, not the venue's own convenience fields.

checkpoints.title: Every MLS team's attacking xG read 0.0 — wrong ASA field name

rules.pass: no team has a real xGA and a zero xGF

checkpoints.resolution: FIXED. `_get_asa_season_stats` tried `xGoals` / `xgoals` / `xgf`, none of which exist on the ASA response — the real field is `xgoals_for`. Meanwhile `xgoals_against` WAS in the defensive fallback list and resolved correctly, so xGA was right and xGF was 0.0 for all 30 teams. Fixed by putting the real key first in both chains. Measured on the 2026-10-28 slate: xGF non-zero on 30/30 teams (median 1.62/game), raw |model-market| median fell from 39.8pp to 3.9pp, MLS produced 15 moneyline picks where it had produced ZERO before, totals went from uniformly 'Under' at the capped +10% to a mixed Over/Under spread at +1.5% to +3.9%, and draw edges fell from a capped +10% to +1.9%.
checkpoints.rationale: ⚠️ THE LESSON IS ONE-SIDED BREAKAGE. This survived because the working half kept the output plausible: with both teams' attack at zero the model still RANKED teams correctly off xGA, so MLS moneylines stayed well calibrated (2.2pp off the market) and nothing on the card looked wrong. Only the absolute goal level was destroyed — expected total goals ~1.3 against a market implying ~2.9 — which is why every total was 'Under' and draws were inflated (two teams projected to score nothing draw 0-0 very often). It was found by asking why MLS produced ONLY Draw and Total picks and never a moneyline, then reading the raw model probability (0.8686 for Under 2.5 against a market 0.395) rather than the post-cap number, which the credibility cap had flattened to a tidy-looking +10%. ⚠️ THE CAP HIDES THE SYMPTOM: a market pinned at exactly the cap on every pick is evidence of a broken input, not of edge. The invariant now asserted is that a team cannot have a real xGA and a zero xGF.

checkpoints.title: CFB priced from Kalshi via an ESPN-anchored slate (last budget sport off the Odds API)

rules.pass: CFB discovers >=90% of ESPN's FBS slate from Kalshi on every run; no game dict where the moneyline and spread disagree on who is favoured; CFB raw |model-market| median stays below 10pp
rules.fail: coverage below 90% on two consecutive Saturdays, OR any moneyline/spread orientation disagreement, OR raw gap median above 10pp (the inflation signature)

checkpoints.rationale: Kalshi's CFB tickers carry a PLACEHOLDER date — KXNCAAFGAME-26OCT30ARIZTTU is Arizona at Texas Tech, which ESPN kicks off 2026-10-31T16:00Z, and occurrence_datetime (03:00Z) is not the kickoff either. Filtering that book by Kalshi's own date drops the entire Saturday slate (36 games read as Friday's) and keeps the wrong ones, so the ticker ORDER cannot be trusted to encode home/away either. The slate is therefore anchored on ESPN — which knows the date, the kickoff, the homeAway flags and the neutral-site flag — and Kalshi supplies only prices, joined by team. Two join keys are needed and neither suffices alone: structural NAME matching resolved 43/47 games on 2026-10-31 and ticker ABBREVIATION resolved a different 40/47 (ESPN says NCSU where Kalshi says NCST; ESPN says 'App State' where Kalshi says 'Appalachian St.'). Together: 52/52 across three measured slates. Measured first run: 47/47 games, 47 moneylines, 12 spreads and 15 totals surviving the 10c liquidity filter (CFB spread/total books have median open interest of ZERO, as cfb.py has documented since Aug), median edge +4.5%, raw |model-market| median 4.6pp, zero moneyline/spread orientation disagreements. ALSO A MODEL INPUT CHANGE: neutral_site was never set on the Odds API path, so every CFB game was silently modelled with a 2.6-point home advantage; ESPN supplies it and 2 of 47 games on the measured slate are genuinely neutral (Notre Dame-Navy, Florida-Georgia). CFB remains watchlist-only — no money is routed either way.

checkpoints.title: Check whether Kalshi lists PER-MATCH IPL markets once the 2027 season starts

rules.pass: a per-match IPL series exists on Kalshi with two-sided quotes → add IPL to KALSHI_PRICEABLE and SPORT_SERIES, and the Odds API can go entirely
rules.fail: only the tournament-winner book exists → IPL still needs the Odds API, which means a free-tier key must be in the ODDS_API_KEY secret before the season

checkpoints.rationale: Verified Oct 29 2026: Kalshi DOES carry IPL, but what is listed is the SEASON OUTRIGHT — event KXIPL-27, ten markets KXIPL-27-<TEAM> titled 'Will <team> win the IPL?', closing 2027-06-20, quoted two-sided (RCB 25/27c, MI 7/8c). Whether a per-match book appears at season start is the open question, and it can only be answered on live data once matches are listed. checkpoints.title: NFL is -7.3pp against the market on outcomes — should it keep real money?
checkpoints.rationale: Opened out of nfl_warm_start's split verdict. NFL budget picks carry real money and NFL is the worst sport we price on outcomes: 43.4% actual against 50.7% market-implied over 242 settled picks since Sep 1 2026 (-7.3pp, ~2.3 s.e.), vs MLB +0.6pp, NBA +1.2pp, NHL -3.5pp. ⚠️ THE CLV GOVERNOR WILL NOT CATCH THIS. NFL's Kalshi CLV is POSITIVE (+0.05pp pool, +0.14pp budget), so every NFL market sits in the governor's keep zone while the outcomes are the worst in the pool. This is the second time our fastest signal has failed to separate winners from losers in a sport (the first being MLB's inverted HIGH-confidence label, Aug 4) and it is the reason a CLV gate alone is not sufficient supervision. Trend is favourable and is the reason for waiting rather than acting now: Sep -11.6pp, Oct -3.7pp, consistent with the Jul 24 warm-start prior decaying out over ~6 games as designed. December covers Weeks 13-18 with every team past the ramp, which is the clean read. Not a broken input: raw |model-market| median 10.9pp and cap firing 33.7% are both in line with NBA and NHL, so this is not the MLS xGF / spread-orientation signature. ⚠️ Do NOT respond by hunting new NFL constants — that is the additive move that has failed repeatedly here. The live options are subtractive: route NFL to watchlist-only (enters_budget=False), or exclude it for Weeks 1-4 next season via BUDGET_EXCLUDED_MARKETS, or leave it and accept the variance. The choice is the user's; it is their money.

Presented with three options (leave / watchlist-only / reduced stake) alongside the -7.3pp finding and the Sep→Oct improvement, and chose to take the December read. ⚠️ This is a DELIBERATE decision, not an unreviewed default: NFL continuing to stake through Nov is the agreed plan, so do not re-raise it as an alarm before 2026-12-07 and do not quietly flip enters_budget. checkpoints.title: MLB per-player hitting stats go empty every January — fix before the 2027 season
checkpoints.rationale: Found while fixing the playerPool bug, verified live: every /stats call in mlb_stats.py queries `season: date.today().year`, and season=2027 returns 0 splits today. So from 2027-01-01 until enough 2027 games are played, all four per-player calls go silently empty again — props back to zero picks, injury value-multipliers back to inert, bullpen stats back to the 4.20/1.30 league fallback (that one at least degrades explicitly). ⚠️ DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED IN THE SAME PASS. The obvious fix — fall back to the previous season — is a MODEL INPUT change, not a plumbing fix, and it interacts badly with the props shrink: shrink_projection weights by n/(n+12) using games played, so handing it a prior season's 150 games would claim a full sample for a player whose role may have changed completely, which is the opposite of what that shrink exists to prevent. It is also the same question as nba_warm_start and nfl_warm_start, and nfl_warm_start has just shown (-7.3pp vs market) that a cold-start prior can be worse than no picks at all. This needs its own deliberate pass with the shrink weighted by CURRENT-season games even when the stat line comes from the prior season — not a one-line fallback. Props carry no money, so the cost of being empty in April is zero picks, which is safe. The injury multiplier is the part that touches money, and it fails toward its old behaviour rather than toward a wrong number.
checkpoints.on_pass: Before the 2027 season opens: either implement prior-season fallback with sample size taken from CURRENT-season games played, or decide explicitly that early-season MLB props and injury multipliers stay dark and record that choice here.
checkpoints.on_fail: If this is reached and nothing was decided, the default is the safe one — stay dark. Do NOT ship a bare prior-season fallback to make the panels look populated.
checkpoints.measurement: Call get_batter_props_stats and get_injury_value_mults for any team in January 2027 and confirm whether they return rows.

checkpoints.title: Does the output-sanity detector earn its place — real catches vs false alarms?
checkpoints.rationale: src/state/model_sanity.py — the first automated check in this project that reads the model's OUTPUT rather than the health of the pipes. Every pre-existing check asks 'is data flowing' (settlement rate, CLV coverage, Kalshi map freshness, log liveness); none asked 'is what the model just produced plausible', which is the single question that would have caught the three most expensive bugs of Oct 2026. The insight it encodes: a real edge is NOISY AND TWO-SIDED; a broken input is CONFIDENT AND ONE-SIDED. So it watches three things per (sport, market) — all picks on one side, the credibility cap firing on nearly everything, and median raw |model-market| beyond anything a working market produces — plus drift of the latter two against each market's OWN trailing baseline, and a market that goes quiet while its siblings keep producing. Thresholds are DERIVED from each market's own history wherever possible. The three absolute floors are not tuning knobs; they are levels at which the output cannot be a working model in any sport. A hand-tuned band would rot exactly like the hardcoded sport lists did. ⚠️ IT DETECTS, IT DOES NOT GATE, and that boundary is tested. Money routing stays with the CLV governor and the user. A noisy detector wired straight to the budget could silently kill a healthy market, which is the exact failure mode this module exists to prevent. BACKTESTED BEFORE SHIPPING: run as of 2026-07-15 it fires on MLS with three independent high-severity signals (100% under, 100% cap-fired, 39.1pp raw gap) against a bug that actually ran undetected from May to October. ⚠️ HONEST MISS: it did NOT catch the Oct 27-28 NBA spread sign inversion — spread pick_side values varied, so the one-sided test never fired, and cap firing at 70% sat under the 85% floor. That bug is covered by TestSpreadOrientation instead. Detection by output shape is a net, not a guarantee. FIRST LIVE CATCH, same day: NBA Total one-sided 63/63, which traced to expected_total running 6.2 points below the market line — recorded on nba_warm_start.
checkpoints.on_pass: If most high-severity findings over the window traced to a real defect, keep it and consider adding the one-sided test for spread markets using the ML/spread favourite agreement instead of pick_side.
checkpoints.on_fail: If it mostly cries wolf, RAISE the floors or drop the weakest signal — do not leave a noisy alert in place. An alert that fires on healthy markets is worse than no alert, because the reader learns to skip it, and that is precisely how the MLS bug survived five months.
checkpoints.measurement: Count high-severity findings in the weekly reports over the window; for each, whether it led to a real fix, a quarantine, or nothing.

checkpoints.title: Outcome governor: second gating arm — does it gate the right things?
checkpoints.rationale: src/state/outcome_governor.py — gates budget routing on OUTCOMES, beside the CLV governor, combined with AND so either arm can block and neither can un-block the other. ⚠️ WHY: every automatic gate read CLV, and CLV missed the worst sport we price. NFL carries POSITIVE CLV (+0.14pp on budget picks, the only positive budget sport) while its picks won 43.4% against a market implying 50.7% — a 7.3pp deficit over 242 settled picks. A single-signal governor is only as good as its blind spot, and this was the second time our fastest signal failed to separate winners from losers (the first being MLB's inverted HIGH-confidence label). METRIC: actual win rate minus the mean market-implied probability of the same picks. Not raw win rate — 45% is excellent on 35c underdogs and terrible on 60c favourites, so only the difference is comparable across markets. THRESHOLDS ARE DERIVED, not tuned: se = sqrt(0.25/n), z = deficit/se, and a market gates only when z <= -2.0 AND deficit <= -2.0pp. Both conditions are load-bearing — z alone would gate a -0.3pp deficit at n=50,000 (real but meaningless), magnitude alone would gate one bad week. The -2.0pp floor also absorbs the residual overround that survives de-vigging, which biases every deficit slightly negative; a floor at zero would eventually gate everything. SPORT-LEVEL AND MARKET-LEVEL both computed, because outcomes are noisy: NFL's three markets hold 91/85/66 settled picks, all far below MIN_N, while the sport holds 242 and is clearly negative. Per-market gating alone would have missed NFL entirely. NFL's markets are -4.4/-6.0/-12.9pp, so the sport-level call is not hiding one bad market behind two good ones. MEASURED ON SHIPPING: 1 real gate (NFL, z=-2.27 — EXEMPT, see below), 1 redundant gate (MLB F5 Total, -5.3pp z=-2.01, already in BUDGET_EXCLUDED_MARKETS so it carries no money and this merely confirms the F5 probation independently), and ZERO false gates across 9 sports. NHL does NOT gate on full history (-1.7pp, z=-0.73, n=483) — the -3.5pp figure measured earlier was a since-Sep window effect, which is a useful reminder to quote the window with the number. ⚠️ THE NFL EXEMPTION is the user's explicit decision of Oct 29, taken with the -7.3pp figure in front of them, and it EXPIRES 2026-12-07 with nfl_budget_probation. Without it NFL gates today. The weekly health report raises an alert for any gate held off by an exemption — an invisible exemption would be worse than no governor, because the panel would claim protection that is not being provided. Do not extend it without a new decision from the user.
checkpoints.on_pass: If the gates it fired were markets we would also have stopped by hand, and nothing healthy was gated, keep it and consider lowering MIN_N as samples grow.
checkpoints.on_fail: If it gated a market that then recovered strongly, RAISE MIN_N or Z_GATE rather than adding exceptions. Gated markets keep producing in display and keep being measured, so recovery is automatic and a wrong gate is recoverable — but a governor nobody trusts gets exemptions bolted on until it does nothing, which is the failure mode to avoid.
checkpoints.measurement: state/outcome_state.json per run, plus the outcome-gate lines in the daily log.
